title.narrative: NEPAL SECOND GREEN, RESILIENT, AND INCLUSIVE PROGRAMMATIC DEVELOPMENT POLICY CREDIT

description.narrative: The Green, Resilient, and Inclusive Development (GRID) programmatic Development Policy Credit (DPC) series is a catalyst for Nepal's ongoing transition to a GRID path. The series of three operations is a key instrument for Nepal to operationalize its homegrown GRID Platform across the economy. This ambition is articulated in the 2021 Kathmandu Declaration on GRID, 2023 Joint CommuniquE on GRID, Nepal's 16th Five-Year Development Plan, and Nepal's GRID Strategic Action Plan 2024-2034 (SAP) which is now being finalized after a series of provincial consultations. The GRID SAP includes over US10 billion dollars of ongoing and pipeline investments for ten key transitions. The World Bank and 15 other Development Partners (DPs) back this effort, including the International Monetary Fund (IMF), International Finance Corporation (IFC), Asian Development Bank (ADB), the United Nations, and other multilateral, bilateral, and nongovernmental organizations that coordinate on policy, knowledge, and investment via Nepal's GRID Platform. Nepal's political situation remains fluid, yet commitment to GRID and this DPC series has been maintained by four successive coalition governments that have taken office since the November 2022 federal and provincial elections. The current coalition took over on July 14, 2024, led by the two largest parties in Parliament. This change has impacted the provincial government set up. At the sub-national level, funds, functions, and staff are managed by the seven provinces and 753 local governments for which legislation, institutions, and administrative procedures have been formalized as constitutionally prescribed. The federalization process is supported by this DPC series.
To improve the enabling environment for Nepal's green, resilient, and inclusive development pathway.

comment.narrative:

Information source: Ministry of Finance/World Bank analysis.

title.narrative: 4. SESAs carried out for policies, programs, and strategic plans

comment.narrative: After substantive TA delivered on policy SESA, draft SESA guidelines have been prepared by the GoN (led by the Ministry of Forests and Environment) after having stock taking exercise and training on SESA to relevant Government officials in March 2025. However, the SESA guidelines have yet to be operationalized. The World Bank, ADB and IFC will be supporting Nepal to operationalize SESA for hydropower projects in Nepal in the near future, but the target for this result indicator will not be achieved by the closing of GRID DPC-2 in December 15, 2025. The draft guidelines will go through sectoral focused group discussions and provincial consultations before finalization. This is expected be completed before the Nepal Government's fiscal year closing in mid-July 2026.

title.narrative: 9B. Operators of WSS services licensed with binding performance indicators for safe water provision

comment.narrative:
Currently there is only one licensed operator. Progress on licensing other operators has been delayed due to the protracted approval of the Regulatory Support Section within Department of Water Supply and Sewerage Management (DWSSM). That section has recently been approved (through a formal O&M process) and budget has been allocated for the current FY. The Section is finalizing the licensing template and documentation, after which they plan to start the roll-out.
The end target of 50 operators by Dec 2026 may not be feasible. The mechanisms through which providers will be licensed remain unclear across all three levels of government. DWSSM, as per the new Regulations, is meant to take on the licensing role, at least for larger water supply projects. The Water Sector Governance and Infrastructure Support Project (P176589) (WASGISP) is supporting the formation of a section within DWSSM to help do this, and aims to pilot the approach of tariff approval and licensing in Birendranagar.

title.narrative: 7. The delivery system of at least one social protection program is used for the provision of relief and recovery in response to a shock

comment.narrative:
The GoN approved the Shock Responsive Social Protection and Relief Distribution Standard 2081 on Jan 1, 2025. However, the results target is yet to be achieved as approved standards are yet to be systematically applied during a disaster. The team is now working with National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) to orient the municipalities to these Standards and help operationalize it. Besides orientation and capacity building of municipalities, operationalizing the Standards entails the following: • Amending the guidelines of the Social Security Allowances (SSA) and National Employment Program (NEP) to align it with SRSP Standards and enable scalability by design • Modifying the Management Information Systems (MISs) of the SSA and NEP to enable it to enroll temporary beneficiaries during times of shock.
Full implementation, however, requires social registry, development of which is still under discussion with MOHA. WB team is working with GoN on these aspects.

title.narrative: 3. People with improved resilience to climate-related disasters due to the installation and operation of additional hydromet monitoring stations and/or radar

comment.narrative:
The Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) installed two additional radars: one in Palpa district and the other in Udaypur district. Additionally, more than 25 hydromet stations have been set up throughout Nepal. The radars and hydromet stations are operational and weather information from these systems are used for the generation of weather forecasts and early warning information.
Based on this, this RI has been achieved, as the population covered by the radar and weather stations amount to more than 5 million. During the 2025 monsoon, DHM sent more than 20 million early warning messages to people at risk of weather-related disasters (floods and heavy rain).
Information source: Department of Hydrology and Meteorology.

title.narrative: 9A. River Basin Offices operationalized with approved river basin plans

comment.narrative: The government approved the establishment of three River Basin Offices (RBOs) in the Koshi, Gandaki, and Karnali River Basins. To operationalize the RBOs: in Biratnagar for Koshi, in Chitwan for Gandaki, and in Surkhet for Karnali, the WECS is awaiting budget approval from the Ministry of Finance. The current plan is to establish and operate these 3 RBOS by the end of Nepali Fiscal Year i.e. July 15, 2026. The WECS is also exploring potential support from various development partners for the operationalization of the RBOs, as well as the implementation of river basin plans. The River Basin Plans for 10 river basins have been prepared by the WECS with the World Bank and Development Partner support. Also, the World Bank recently supported WECS in capacity building for river basin governance based on IWRM principles and to promote stakeholder engagement at the river basin level.

title.narrative: 5. Tourism concessions awarded to conservation-based enterprises under the National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Regulation

comment.narrative: While significant progress was made in reforming the concession framework for protected areas that will allow for nature-based tourism opportunities for private sector operators, this reform is very recent. Potential concessions may occur in the future if and when the reform gains traction. In August 2025, the government introduced a sixth amendment to the National Parks and Wildlife Act (2030 Bikram Sambat), which is pending approval. This amendment would: • Open concessions to a wider range of investments (e.g., eco-tourism, cable cars, hydropower). • Emphasize biodiversity offsets, require Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA), and establish a Wildlife Conservation Fund. • Strengthen the role of Buffer Zone Committees and promotes direct benefits for Indigenous Peoples and local communities. The amendment alone would not contribute towards the achievement of the Result as the corresponding regulation must still be developed, endorsed and operationalized.
